global.definition: State-run database of dispensed controlled-substance prescriptions. Prescribers query before issuing or refilling Schedule II–V medications to surface concurrent prescribers, early fills, and overdose risk. Many states (e.g. MA, NJ) call theirs the PMP.
New York's PDMP. Mandatory query before every Schedule II–IV prescription. New Jersey's analog is the NJPMP.
New Jersey's PDMP. Mandatory query at initial prescribing of any controlled substance and at least quarterly during ongoing therapy.
Opioid dose normalized to oral morphine. CDC 2022 flags ≥50 MME/day for caution and ≥90 MME/day as high-risk; thresholds inform monitoring, not absolute caps.
DSM-5 diagnosis. Treated as a chronic medical condition; first-line pharmacotherapy is buprenorphine, methadone, or naltrexone (collectively MOUD).
DSM-5 diagnosis. Pharmacotherapy options include naltrexone, acamprosate, and disulfiram; gabapentin and topiramate are evidence-supported off-label.

Buprenorphine, methadone, and naltrexone. Also called Opioid Agonist Therapy (OAT) when restricted to agonists/partial agonists, or Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT) — the older umbrella term being phased out per SAMHSA guidance. ASAM 2025 and CDC 2022 emphasize that MOUD is not withheld for concurrent benzodiazepine use — co-management is preferred over discontinuation.
Federally-licensed clinic that dispenses methadone (and increasingly buprenorphine) for OUD. Methadone for OUD must be dispensed via an OTP; buprenorphine can be office-prescribed.
Federal statute (21 USC §801 et seq.) classifying controlled substances into Schedules I–V and setting prescribing rules. Implementing regulations live at 21 CFR §1300 et seq.
The codified rules of US federal agencies. Controlled-substance prescribing rules live at 21 CFR §1300–1321.
The codified federal statutes. The Controlled Substances Act is codified at 21 USC §801 et seq.
Federal agency that registers prescribers and enforces the Controlled Substances Act. DEA registration is required to prescribe Schedule II–V medications.
Federal agency responsible for drug approvals and labeling. The boxed warning (formerly 'black box') is the FDA's strongest labeling caution.

global.expansion: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
global.definition: US public health agency. Publishes the 2016 / 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain.
US specialty society for addiction medicine. Co-published the 2024–2025 ASAM/ACMT Clinical Practice Guideline on Benzodiazepine Tapering.
US specialty society for family medicine. Frequent source of plain-language clinical reviews cited by primary-care decision support.

global.expansion: American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
global.definition: US specialty society for child and adolescent psychiatry. Authors the youth ADHD and SUD practice parameters.
US specialty society for addiction psychiatry. Frequent co-author with ASAM on opioid, benzodiazepine, and SUD guidelines.
US specialty society for pediatrics. Co-authors pediatric ADHD guidance with AACAP and places ADHD titration squarely in primary-care scope.
US specialty society for geriatrics. Publishes the Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medications in older adults (2023 update).
US specialty society for neurology. Authors the practice guidelines on mild cognitive impairment (MCI).
Federal panel that grades evidence for preventive services. Recommendations carry letter grades A–D and 'I' for insufficient.

global.expansion: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
global.definition: UK clinical guideline body. Often referenced for ADHD and chronic-pain pathways where US guidance is less specific.
Joint US clinical practice guideline series. Authoritative on opioid therapy, benzodiazepines, SUD, and chronic pain.
DSM-5 neurodevelopmental disorder. First-line pharmacotherapy in adults and adolescents is stimulants (methylphenidate or amphetamine class).
DSM-5 anxiety disorder. First-line pharmacotherapy is SSRI/SNRI; benzodiazepines are second-line and not for chronic monotherapy.
Cognitive decline beyond expected aging without dementia-level functional impairment. Per AAN, benzodiazepines and other anticholinergic / sedating agents should be deprescribed where possible.
Parasomnia involving dream enactment. One of the named exceptions where chronic clonazepam may be appropriate despite the Beers Criteria.
DSM-5 trauma- and stressor-related disorder. Benzodiazepines are not recommended for PTSD per VA-DoD; first-line is trauma-focused psychotherapy plus SSRI/SNRI.
DSM-5 anxiety-spectrum disorder. First-line pharmacotherapy is SSRI at higher doses; benzodiazepines are not effective monotherapy.
Class of antidepressants (sertraline, escitalopram, fluoxetine, paroxetine, citalopram). First-line for most depressive and anxiety disorders.
Class of antidepressants (venlafaxine, duloxetine, desvenlafaxine). First-line alongside SSRIs for depression, GAD, and some chronic pain conditions.
Older antidepressant class. Rarely used in primary care due to dietary tyramine restrictions and serotonin-syndrome risk with serotonergic agents.

global.expansion: Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol — Revised
global.definition: 10-item scored scale for alcohol withdrawal severity. Drives symptom-triggered benzodiazepine dosing during inpatient detox.
11-item scored scale for opioid withdrawal severity. Score ≥8 generally signals readiness for buprenorphine induction.

global.expansion: Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test — Concise
global.definition: 3-question screen for unhealthy alcohol use. Positive thresholds: ≥4 in men, ≥3 in women.
Self-report screen and severity measure for GAD. Cutoffs: 5 mild, 10 moderate, 15 severe.
Self-report screen and severity measure for major depression. Score ≥10 supports a depression diagnosis pending clinical interview.
The patient's principal clinician — typically family medicine, internal medicine, or pediatrics. PCP and PCC are used interchangeably in some institutional documents.

AGS list of potentially inappropriate medications in adults ≥65. 2023 update flags benzodiazepines as a general avoid with named exceptions (seizure, RBD, catatonia, treatment-resistant GAD, palliative).
DSM-5 diagnostic category covering disordered use of alcohol, opioids, stimulants, cannabis, sedatives, and other substances. Severity is graded mild / moderate / severe by criterion count.
DSM-5 diagnosis for problematic cannabis use. No FDA-approved pharmacotherapy; behavioral therapy (CBT, motivational enhancement) is first-line.

Third-party administrator (CVS Caremark, Express Scripts, OptumRx) that sets formularies, fill quantities, and early-fill thresholds for insured prescriptions. PBM thresholds are operational, not clinical guidelines.

global.expansion: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
global.definition: US federal agency that regulates Opioid Treatment Programs and publishes the TIP and TAP series of clinical guidance for SUD treatment.
18-item self-report screen for adult ADHD. The 6-item Part A is widely used as the screen — score ≥4 suggests further evaluation. Distinct from ADHD-RS (clinician-rated).
Clinician-rated 18-item severity scale based on DSM criteria. Used in trials to track response. Distinct from the ASRS (self-report) and from the ADHD diagnosis itself.
Dose at which 95% of subjects achieve the intended pharmacologic effect. Cited in stimulant titration and benzodiazepine equivalence work.
Effect-size measure from logistic regression and case-control studies. OR=1 means no association; OR>1 means the exposure increases the odds of the outcome.
Odds ratio after adjustment for confounding variables in a regression model. Often written aOR in primary literature.
Effect-size measure from Cox proportional-hazards survival models, after adjustment for confounders. Often written aHR in primary literature.
Study design where subjects are randomly assigned to intervention or control. Highest level of evidence for efficacy questions.

global.expansion: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology
global.definition: Joint authors of the cholesterol, hypertension, and ASCVD prevention guidelines used in primary care.
US specialty society for psychiatry. Publishes the DSM (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual) and clinical practice guidelines.

global.expansion: American Pain Society / American Academy of Pain Medicine
global.definition: Joint authors of the 2009 opioid-prescribing guideline for chronic non-cancer pain (since superseded by CDC 2016 / 2022).

global.expansion: American College of Occupational and Environmental Medicine
global.definition: US specialty society for occupational and environmental medicine. Publishes return-to-work guidance for opioid- and benzodiazepine-related impairment.

global.expansion: HIV Medicine Association / Infectious Diseases Society of America
global.definition: Joint authors of clinical guidance on opioid prescribing and SUD management in patients with HIV.

Patient–prescriber written contract covering controlled-substance prescribing rules — single prescriber, single pharmacy, UDS expectations, early-refill policy. Documents informed consent without limiting clinical judgment.
Bedside or in-office testing (POC urine drug screen, POC ultrasound) as opposed to send-out lab work. POC immunoassay UDS panels need confirmatory testing for clinical decisions.
Confirmatory lab method for urine drug testing. Resolves false positives from immunoassay panels; older platform now largely replaced by LC-MS/MS.
Modern confirmatory urine drug testing platform. More sensitive than GC-MS for many compounds and the standard for low-cutoff confirmatory testing.

global.expansion: Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription medication, and other Substance use
global.definition: NIDA's two-stage SUD screening tool used in primary care. TAPS-1 is the brief screen; TAPS-2 follows up positives with substance-specific questions.
10-item self-report screen for non-alcohol drug use. Positive at score ≥3.
NIH institute for substance use research. Publishes the TAPS screen, the NIDA Quick Screen, and clinical reviews.
Zolpidem, zaleplon, and eszopiclone. Bind the same GABA-A receptor site as benzodiazepines and share many of the same Beers concerns, falls risk, and complex sleep behaviors.
US specialty society for medical toxicology. Co-author with ASAM on the 2024–2025 benzodiazepine tapering guideline.
Driving-simulator and on-road measure of lane weaving. Primary outcome in benzodiazepine and Z-drug driving-impairment studies; equivalent to a 0.05% blood-alcohol effect at threshold.

US DOT agency that regulates commercial driving. Disqualifies CDL holders for many controlled-substance prescriptions; relevant to occupational return-to-work decisions for opioid- and benzodiazepine-treated patients.
3-item pain scale (each 0–10) tracking chronic pain severity, enjoyment-of-life impact, and general-activity impact. Used for primary-care follow-up; sensitive to change.
Functional assessment domain (bathing, dressing, eating, transferring, toileting, continence). Used in geriatric assessment and trials of cognition or sedating medications.
